strengths: Clear and intuitive core observation linking embedding dispersion to model perplexity, well-motivated and clearly presented
Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple model families (LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi) and domains (WikiText, CNN DailyMail, PubMed) with strong correlations (r=-0.60 to -0.93)
Multiple practical applications demonstrated beyond characterization: downstream performance prediction, model selection, layer selection for kNN-LM, and training signal
Rigorous experimental design with fine-grained analysis (semantic clusters in §3.3), layer-wise progression, fine-tuning effects, and thorough reproducibility details
Excellent presentation of empirical results with comprehensive visualizations and extensive supplementary materials including algorithms and hyperparameters
weaknesses: Limited novelty: connection between embedding geometry and performance is established (Ethayarajh 2019, Gao et al. 2019); Viswanathan et al. [2025] already analyzes token-level distributions; this work refines with specific metric but core insight is incremental

Causality not established: strong correlations shown but assumed causality; auxiliary loss experiments show only marginal improvements (1-4 PPL points single-domain; large improvements only on tiny GPT-2 Small model)

Lack of theoretical foundation: no principled explanation for why cosine distance specifically predicts perplexity; alternative geometric metrics (intrinsic dimension, rank, condition number) not compared; Figure 4 shows correlation substantially weakens with context length (0.89→0.55), undermining universality claims

Application 1 (downstream prediction §4.1): experimental setup artificially varies fraction correct from pre-partitioned pools, not reflecting real distribution shift; no comparison to actual model variants or natural error patterns

Application 2 (model selection §4.2): dispersion gap metric (G = within(T) + between(T,T̄)) appears ad-hoc without ablation or justification; requires manual domain-specific token selection limiting generalizability; no comparison to simpler baselines; claimed 'perfect ranking' on only 9 checkpoints
Application 3 (kNN-LM §4.3): limited to small GPT-2 models (82M-774M); no actual kNN-LM perplexity improvements measured, only layer selection shown; unclear if extends to larger models

Application 4 (training signal §4.4): marginal improvements on small models only (1-4 PPL single-domain); no comparison to alternative regularization or contrastive learning; no experiments on large models where improvements matter

Missing key ablations and comparisons: no comparison to other geometric metrics; no statistical confidence intervals on correlations; no comparison to prior layer-selection methods; sensitivity analysis for binning procedure absent

strengths: Comprehensive empirical validation across diverse model families (LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi) and domains with consistent negative correlations (r = -0.50 to -0.93)
Thorough experimental design including layer-wise analysis, fine-tuning effects, semantic clustering validation, and well-motivated sampling procedures (Algorithm 1)
Multiple practical applications demonstrated with reasonable quantitative results (Spearman ρ > 0.95 for model selection across variants)
Clear presentation with intuitive motivation and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Directly addresses potential confounds through semantic clustering analysis (§3.3) showing both within- and between-cluster dispersion increases
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Builds incrementally on established work on anisotropy and rank collapse (Ethayarajh 2019, Gao et al. 2019); relationship to concurrent work (Viswanathan et al. 2025) underexplored; conceptual advance is primarily systematization

No mechanistic explanation for why dispersion predicts performance; circular intuition in Figure 1 doesn't explain why networks learn dispersed representations; training experiments show correlation but not causation
Training experiments severely limited in scope: only GPT-2-small tested, improvements modest (1-4 ppl points single-domain), no validation on modern LLMs where practical impact would be demonstrated

Model selection application uses static token embeddings (not contextual), different from main analysis; dispersion gap metric is ad-hoc without justification; requires manual domain-specific token lists; limited to Qwen/Llama on specific domains

Downstream performance prediction (§4.1) uses artificial protocol mixing correct/incorrect predictions with fixed input distribution; doesn't test realistic held-out generalization; practical improvements over baselines unquantified
Metric selection unjustified: why average pairwise cosine distance over intrinsic dimension, effective rank, spectral properties? No ablations or comparisons with alternative geometric metrics
Inconsistent correlations across domains (e.g., r = -0.25 for medical domain, Llama-3.1-8B); paper emphasizes consistency but doesn't adequately address substantial variance
kNN-LM layer selection (§4.3) only tested on GPT-2 models (~100M params), not modern retrieval systems using much larger models
Significant limitations acknowledged but unaddressed: English-only, limited domains, final-layer representations only, causality cannot be established, and scoping reduces generalizability

strengths: Clear and well-demonstrated empirical finding: Strong negative correlations (r = -0.60 to -0.92) between representation dispersion and perplexity across diverse models (LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi) and domains (WikiText, CNN DailyMail, PubMed)

Comprehensive empirical analysis including layer-wise progression, within-cluster analysis during training, fine-tuning effects (LoRA vs. full), and multiple granularities (sequence-level, last-token, varying context lengths)

Strong practical application for model selection: Achieves Spearman correlation r > 0.95 for ranking model variants without labels; perfect ranking demonstrated on MATH (Qwen) and HumanEval (CodeLlama)
Excellent presentation and reproducibility: Clear writing, effective visualizations (especially Figure 1), extensive appendices with full hyperparameters, multiple datasets and models tested

Novel within-cluster finding (§3.3): Demonstrates that even semantically similar contexts become more dispersed during training, not just dissimilar examples, providing non-obvious evidence for the claim
Multiple practical applications: Label-free diagnostics, efficient layer selection for kNN-LM (~5K tokens), and downstream accuracy prediction without labeled data
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: The observation that better models have more dispersed representations is intuitive and follows naturally from prior work on embedding anisotropy (Ethayarajh 2019, Gao et al. 2019); primarily characterizes an existing phenomenon rather than proposing novel mechanisms

Causality remains unclear: Demonstrates strong correlation but not whether dispersion causes better performance or is merely symptomatic; the 'push-away' loss evidence is suggestive but shows modest single-domain improvements (1-4 perplexity points) and unexplained cross-domain variation (~20 points)

Missing critical ablations and comparisons: No comparison to alternative geometric metrics (intrinsic dimension, effective rank, spectral analysis); no justification for why average pairwise cosine distance specifically; limited analysis of layer choice; the 'dispersion gap' metric appears ad-hoc

Modest practical improvements for training objective (§4.4): Single-domain gains are small (1-4 points); cross-domain gains much larger (~20 points Wiki, ~10 points Code) but mechanism unexplained; unclear whether improvements are from dispersion specifically or general regularization

Limited generalization scope: Primarily English text, standard benchmarks, limited specialized domains (code, math, medical only briefly); no testing on other languages, modalities, or domain-specific corpora; Appendix C acknowledges but doesn't address

Section 4.1 design concerns: Artificial sampling protocol (fixing correct/incorrect fraction) doesn't reflect realistic deployment; considerable scatter in Figure 8 despite monotonic trend; unclear if better than simpler confidence measures

Section 4.2 applicability limited: Requires knowing task-relevant tokens in advance (digits for math, code keywords); only evaluated on two task families; unclear how to extend to general-purpose tasks; uses pre-trained embeddings not contextual representations

Weakening correlation with context length (Figure 4): Dispersion-perplexity correlation degrades from r = -0.89 (16 tokens) to r = -0.55 (256 tokens) but this important degradation is not explained or investigated

Lack of theoretical understanding: No clear explanation of why dispersion should improve perplexity; no connection to information theory, loss landscape, or generalization theory; mechanism remains opaque despite strong empirical correlation

Incomplete layer selection analysis (§4.3): Only tested on GPT-2 with kNN-LM; unclear generalization to other models/retrieval methods; attention consistently more dispersed than FFN but why is unexplored

strengths: Comprehensive empirical validation across multiple model families (Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi) and domains (WikiText, news, medical) with consistent negative correlations between dispersion and perplexity (r = -0.5 to -0.93)
Well-designed experiments with proper controls including uniform perplexity binning, semantic cluster analysis, and ablation study ('squeeze' experiment) that supports causal claims
Four practical applications demonstrated without labeled data: example hardness ranking, model selection via dispersion gap, layer selection for kNN-LM, and training objective
Strong experimental rigor with held-out test set validation, multiple random seeds, error bars, Vendi Score robustness check, and extensive reproducible details
Clear presentation with good intuitive motivation and comprehensive supplementary materials
weaknesses: Limited novelty: connection between embedding geometry and model quality established in prior work (Ethayarajh 2019, Gao et al. 2019); this paper is an incremental quantification of known phenomena
Correlation vs. causation not definitively established: while 'squeeze' ablation is suggestive, alternative explanations remain (dispersion as symptom rather than cause); mechanism unexplored

Weak theoretical contribution: paper provides no mechanistic insight into why dispersion improves perplexity; intuition ('clearer distinctions enable sharper predictions') is hand-wavy without formal analysis
Narrow scope of training experiments: only GPT-2 on WikiText tested; improvements modest (1-4 points); unclear why practitioners should add another loss term for incremental gains
Simple and potentially incomplete metric: average pairwise cosine distance may miss important geometric properties (intrinsic dimension, alignment); no comparison to alternative geometric measures
Model selection application requires domain-specific tokens identified a priori; limited guidance on how to choose tokens for new domains
Limited downstream evaluation: focus on perplexity; generalization to classification, QA, other tasks unclear; do applications work for non-LM tasks?
Missing analysis of when correlation breaks down: no failure mode discussion, no exploration of architectures where dispersion ≠ quality
Ablations incomplete: hyperparameter sensitivity for λ not thoroughly explored; controlled slicing experiment could introduce bias when sampling extreme accuracy fractions

strengths: Comprehensive empirical evaluation across multiple model families (LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi), domains (WikiText, CNN DailyMail, PubMed), and model scales
Well-designed controlled experiments, particularly the slicing methodology with fixed input distributions and semantic cluster analysis showing both within/between-cluster dispersion increases
Strong and consistent empirical evidence: correlations range from -0.62 to -0.92 across most conditions
Proposes multiple applications beyond correlation (example ranking, model selection, layer selection, training signal)
Extensive supplementary materials with thorough ablations and robustness checks
weaknesses: Central overclaim of causality: paper uses language suggesting 'predictive power' and causal influence when evidence is purely correlational; squeeze ablation doesn't establish causation
Limited novelty: builds incrementally on well-established embedding geometry observations (anisotropy, rank collapse); average pairwise cosine distance is a straightforward metric choice
No theoretical insight into mechanisms: lacks explanation for why dispersion should matter for next-token prediction or what properties dispersed representations enable

Practical applications underwhelming: (1) example hardness ranking shows perplexity nearly flat yet claims label-free advantage; (2) model selection requires domain-specific token selection; (3) layer selection specialized to niche kNN-LM; (4) training improvements (1-4 ppl) modest and not compared to existing methods

Experimental concerns: high correlations (r=-0.92) may reflect binning artifacts; uniform sampling scheme robustness not tested; semantic cluster definition via 10-grams is crude; limited to small-scale training experiments (GPT-2 Small)

Generalization limits: scope restricted to autoregressive English LMs; inconsistent correlations across models (Qwen -0.85 vs Medical-LLaMA -0.25); unclear if findings extend to encoder models, fine-tuned models, or other modalities

Missing critical comparisons: no evaluation against alternative geometry metrics (intrinsic dimension, effective rank, participation ratio); no comparison to baseline methods for proposed applications; limited engagement with related work on embedding isotropy
Surprise result unexplored: Table 3-4 showing perplexity nearly flat across accuracy levels contradicts core premise and deserves investigation rather than claiming label-free advantage

strengths: Strong empirical validation across diverse model families (LLaMA, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, Phi), domains (WikiText, CNN Daily News, PubMed), and model sizes with consistent correlations (r = -0.47 to -0.92)

Comprehensive analysis including layer-wise progression, semantic cluster analysis (Figure 7) showing both within and between-cluster dispersion increases, fine-tuning effects, and held-out generalization

Four practical applications with demonstrated utility: label-free hardness ranking with monotonic relationships, model selection with Spearman ρ > 0.95 perfect rankings, efficient kNN-LM layer selection, and training improvements (especially in cross-domain scenarios)

Direct evidence for causality: ablation study (squeeze experiment) shows clustering embeddings hurts performance by 18+ perplexity points; training trajectory analysis on Olmo-7B with 30 checkpoints shows ρ=0.90-0.95
Methodologically rigorous with uniform perplexity binning, multiple random seeds, error bars throughout, detailed hyperparameters, and honest discussion of limitations
Thorough reproducibility with 38-page appendix, full experimental protocols, and code availability promised; comparison to perplexity as hardness signal showing dispersion outperforms
Clear intuitive presentation with well-motivated figures that establish core ideas early and structured narrative from observation to applications
weaknesses: Primarily observational without mechanistic explanation: lacks theoretical understanding of why dispersion correlates with perplexity; unclear if correlation is causal or both consequences of deeper training dynamics

Metric choice under-justified: why average pairwise cosine distance specifically over other geometric properties (L2 distance, spectral methods, intrinsic dimension)? Vendi Score validation helpful but limited

Causality direction unclear despite ablation support: does high dispersion cause low perplexity or vice versa? Auxiliary loss gains modest in single-domain setting (1-4 ppl) raises questions about practical importance

Limited experimental scope: training improvements tested only on GPT-2-SMALL (scaling unknown), cross-domain training only WikiText+code, multilingual results present but underemphasized, only decoder-only Transformers tested, no non-English language focus

Application limitations: model selection requires manual domain-specific token selection and works only within family/tokenizer; hardness ranking requires forward passes; kNN-LM has limited practical adoption; training improvements are incremental

Missing comparisons: no comparison to other embedding quality metrics (entropy, uncertainty quantification, calibration, rank, intrinsic dimension); related work on anisotropy/rank collapse cited but not deeply engaged

Ad-hoc design choices: dispersion gap formula weights within(T) and between equally without justification; final layer choice appears arbitrary; semantic clustering analysis depends on specific 10-gram artifact

Presentation issues: title slightly overclaims ('predictive power' vs. correlation); notation inconsistencies (D vs D-bar); figure overplotting in scatter plots; some standard errors large for smaller models
